claims.claim: Added a versioned, closed, bounded checkpoint request API with native TASK/RUN/operation, committed candidate/tree, scope and reviewed-plan authentication.

Sealing reopens native Runtime observations and raw captures, preserving full reviewed proof coverage, original evidence identities, outcomes, outstanding obligations and resource facts independently of PLANNED status or Executor claims.
Checkpoint history enforces predecessor-free K1, consecutive ordinals, exact predecessor digests, distinct descendant candidates and preserved semantic and execution populations.

Runtime-owned exclusive mutation fences, immutable flushed records, cumulative accounting and original capture hashes provide read-only exact replay and block conflicting, interrupted, stale or unknown effects.

Explicit terminal completion reauthenticates the final satisfactory checkpoint and consumes its original current-RUN evidence without equivalent verification execution; distinct mandatory proof remains required and unsupported comparisons remain blocked.

Checkpoint and terminal effects share Runtime exclusion with existing completion and failure ownership; exact terminal replay reconciles persisted bytes, conflicting or late effects block, and REPAIR/REMEDIATION requests cannot inherit PRIMARY authority.

Added real-Git/native subprocess conformance definitions covering first and second checkpoints, terminal reuse, full coverage, replay, collisions, crashes, terminal exclusion and stale, unknown and correction adversarial cases without affirmative authentication mocks.

Committed changes in exactly the six authorized files, retained default V1/V2 verification branches, and documented F_i, leased continuation, G3/G6, production cutover and L4 measurements as NOT_ACTIVATED/OUTSTANDING.
